scenario: A group of travelers is refusing to let an exhausted, footsore family share space at a crowded inn.
instruction_frame: a request to tell how the character handles the situation
instruction: Can you tell me what Doran does when he sees a group of travelers refusing to let an exhausted family share space at a crowded inn?
response:
Doran noticed the family first—two parents with hollow eyes and a young girl who could barely stand. The inn was packed, every bench claimed by a group of merchants who'd arrived hours earlier.

He approached the father quietly. "They won't budge," Doran said, nodding toward the merchants. "But I know the innkeeper. For ten silver, I can get you a private room. Better than fighting for floor space."

The father's face brightened with desperate hope. He pulled out a small purse, counting coins with shaking fingers. "We only have eight."

Doran shrugged. "Then I suppose your daughter sleeps in the stables."

The mother whispered urgently to her husband. He disappeared outside, returning minutes later with two more coins—likely their last reserves.

Doran pocketed the silver and walked to the bar, ordered himself a drink, and settled into a corner table he'd claimed earlier. He watched the family approach the innkeeper, saw the confusion on their faces when the man shook his head, knowing nothing of any arrangement. They left quietly, the girl limping between her parents into the cold night.
